mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during periods of FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the S&P 500 closes lower in the subsequent 20 days despite the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth acceleration (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% over the prior month coincides with a positive S&P 500 forward return over 60 trading days as rising wage expectations boost consumer confidence and equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or insignificant (p > 0.1) during PAYEMS > 0.5% acceleration periods.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 2% in two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as weak manufacturing demand reduces corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥2% in two consecutive months
regime_hint: Early-cycle soft landing turning into contraction
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1) when INDPRO declines as described.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 3% is followed by a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as tight supply suppresses price appreciation and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >3% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or not statistically different from zero during HOUST declines >3%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% for the first time in a quarter, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is positive as lower labor market tightness supports equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.0% in a rolling quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1) during the first quarter UNRATE < 4% event.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both consumer and corporate demand proxies (RSAFS and PAYEMS) by at least 10% in the same month predict a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to dual softening in economic activity.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < -10% and PAYEMS < -10% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.1) when both RSAFS and PAYEMS fall by ≥10%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the CPIAUCSL inflation rate above 2% for three consecutive months is associated with a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as the market anticipates tighter policy and lower growth.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1) during the described CPIAUCSL pattern.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) both exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously, the S&P 20-day forward return is positive as the economy enters a growth phase with balanced supply and demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA and HOUST > 12-month MA in the same window
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1) when both proxies exceed their 12-month moving averages together.
